title: Dragging a placed enemy can fire the cell click after the drop
body:
## Summary
SpatialGrid captures the pointer on the dragged enemy cell and clears isDragging in pointerup, so the click that follows a drag arrives with isDragging already false.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/SpatialGrid.tsx:42 sets pointer capture on the enemy cell; handlePointerUp (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/SpatialGrid.tsx:67-91) clears isDragging and dispatches moveEnemy; the enemy cell onClick (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/SpatialGrid.tsx:121) guards on !isDragging, which is already false. Cells are keyed by index (:117), so after the move the same DOM node can carry the empty-cell onPlace handler (:172). Fixed = a moved-during-drag ref set on pointermove past a threshold and consumed by onClick.

## Flow
- press an enemy, drag it to another cell, release
- pointerup dispatches moveEnemy; the click is retargeted to the captured node
- expected in a real browser: the enemy is removed, or a new one is placed at the source cell

## Expected impact
Designers moving enemies would get phantom placements or removals, measurable as extra history entries per drag. Risk: a threshold set too high breaks click-to-remove.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one drag produces exactly one draft edit
Before: not measured: jsdom does not retarget click under pointer capture
After: predicted 1 edit per drag
Method: simulation - walked the handler order; the rung above needs a real-browser pointer sequence
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Playwright probe on the Encounter tab: drag e1 to an empty cell, assert history grows by exactly 1 and the enemy count is unchanged

title: Spatial grid placement, removal and move are pointer-only
body:
## Summary
All 24 SpatialGrid cells are plain divs with onClick/onPointerDown and none is focusable, so an encounter cannot be built from the keyboard.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/SpatialGrid.tsx:117, :136, :152 and :167 render div cells with click handlers and no role, tabIndex or key handler (0 of 24 focusable). Fixed = a roving-tabindex grid (role=grid/gridcell), Enter/Space to place or remove, arrow keys to move focus, modifier+arrow to move an enemy.

## Flow
- Tab into the Encounter editor
- focus skips the whole grid
- fix: roving tabindex and key handlers, then a test counting focusable cells

## Expected impact
Keyboard and switch users can author encounters. Risk: an interaction rewrite in a 190-line file near the 200 LOC rule.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - keyboard-operable grid
Before: 0 of 24 cells focusable (rendered grid)
After: 24 of 24 reachable with one tab stop (predicted)
Method: probe - counted focusable cells on the rendered grid; the After needs the rewrite built in isolation
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: render SpatialGrid, assert exactly one tabIndex=0 cell, ArrowRight moves focus, Enter on an empty cell calls onPlace

title: Seven tuning sliders have no accessible name
body:
## Summary
TuningSlider shows its label in a sibling span and the shared StyledSlider has no aria-label pass-through, so all 7 Tuning Overrides range inputs are unnamed.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/TuningSlider.tsx:23 renders the label as a span; src/components/ui/StyledSlider.tsx:47 renders the range input with no aria-label prop. The fix needs an ariaLabel prop on the shared StyledSlider, which is outside this context (out-of-scope seam).

## Flow
- render TuningPanel
- query input[type=range]: 7 of 7 unnamed
- add StyledSlider ariaLabel and pass the label from TuningSlider

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users hear "slider" seven times with no name. Touches a shared ui primitive used elsewhere.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - named tuning sliders
Before: 7 of 7 unnamed
After: 0 of 7 (predicted)
Method: probe - read the rendered DOM; the fix site is src/components/ui (out of scope)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Timeline scrub and wave selection are pointer-only
body:
## Summary
The UnifiedTimeline scrub area and the WaveManager wave rows are click-only divs, so neither the playhead nor the selected wave can be changed from the keyboard.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/UnifiedTimeline.tsx:102 handles click and pointermove on a div with no role or key handler; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/panels.tsx:41-44 selects a wave through a div onClick. Fixed = role=slider with aria-valuenow and arrow keys on the timeline; wave rows as buttons or a listbox (the nested spawn-time input needs care).

## Flow
- Tab through the Encounter editor
- no stop on the timeline or on the wave rows
- fix, then key-driven component tests

## Expected impact
Keyboard users can scrub and pick waves. Risk: nesting an input inside an interactive row.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - keyboard scrub and wave select
Before: 0 focusable scrub targets; 0 of 3 wave rows focusable
After: 1 slider; 3 of 3 rows (predicted)
Method: probe - counted on the rendered DOM; the After needs the build
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: ArrowRight on the timeline slider calls onScrub(t + step); Enter on wave row 2 calls onSelect(1)

title: Balance alerts flash and scroll only when the alert count changes
body:
## Summary
BalanceAlertsPanel runs its critical flash and scroll-into-view only when alerts.length differs from the previous render, so a pass that swaps one finding for a new critical of equal count draws no attention.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/BalanceAlertsPanel.tsx:24-38 compares against prevAlertsLen only; rows are keyed by index (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/BalanceAlertsPanel.tsx:78), so React also reuses row nodes across different findings. Fixed = key rows by kind+time and trigger on a change in the set of critical kinds.

## Flow
- tune so a spongy warning becomes a player-death critical with the count unchanged
- no flash and no scroll
- fix: diff critical-kind sets between renders

## Expected impact
A newly critical finding is always surfaced. Low risk.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a new critical finding is always surfaced
Before: predicted 0 flashes on an equal-count swap
After: predicted 1
Method: simulation - walked the effect; needs a two-render component test with crafted alerts
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: component test: rerender with same-length alerts containing a new critical, assert scrollIntoView called once

title: Encounter export ships HealingMul the editor can neither tune nor simulate
body:
## Summary
generateUE5Export writes all 8 TuningOverrides keys, the TuningPanel exposes 7 (no healingMul) and simulateEncounter reads healingMul 0 times.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/ue5-export.ts:53 emits HealingMul; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/panels.tsx:126-132 render 7 sliders; src/lib/combat/choreography-sim.ts has 0 reads of healingMul (rg). The export asserts a tuned value nothing in this editor produced. Fixed = drop it from the encounter export, or add the slider and make the sim honour it - a choice, so it is pinned by a key-parity test either way.

## Flow
- open Tuning Overrides: no healing slider
- export: HealingMul = 1.00f
- decide, then pin export keys == tunable keys == sim-read keys

## Expected impact
The exported config matches what was actually tuned and simulated.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - export / UI / sim key parity
Before: export 8 keys, UI 7, sim reads healingMul 0 times
After: all three equal
Method: probe - grep counts; which side moves is a decision the instrument does not make
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: unit test: UPROPERTY keys in generateUE5Export output equal the TuningPanel slider keys and the keys simulateEncounter reads

title: Attribute row variable names are derived unsanitised from rowName
body:
## Summary
buildAttributeDefaultsPython names each Python variable row_<lowercased rowName> and quotes rowName raw, so a row named "Elite Knight" or containing a quote emits invalid Python.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/attributes/attribute-defaults-export.ts:64-66 (rowVar) and the add_data_table_row literal. Today the rows are the 3 fixed seeds (Player, Skeleton, Boss) and AttributeDefaultsTab cannot rename them, so the defect is latent. Fixed = sanitise to [a-z0-9_] with an index suffix and JSON-quote the literal.

## Flow
- call buildAttributeDefaultsPython with rowName "Elite Knight"
- emits "row_elite knight = ..." - a SyntaxError
- fix and add a unit test

## Expected impact
Goes live the moment row names become editable or come from the catalog.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - any rowName yields valid Python
Before: predicted 1 SyntaxError per spaced name
After: 0
Method: simulation - the input is unreachable from the current UI
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: unit test with rowNames ["Elite Knight", "Boss's"] asserting every row variable matches ^row_[a-z0-9_]+$

title: UE5 encounter export declares a USTRUCT but writes spawn rows as comments
body:
## Summary
generateUE5Export declares FEncounterSpawnEntry but emits every spawn row and wave as // comments and the tuning as bare UPROPERTY lines outside any class, so the downloaded EncounterConfig.h gives UE nothing to import.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/choreography/ue5-export.ts:17-27 emit the struct, :34-41 comment lines per enemy and wave, :46-53 dangling UPROPERTYs. A usable hand-off (a DataTable via a UE Python script, as attribute-defaults-export.ts already does) is a contract with the UE project outside this tree.

## Flow
- Export .h
- paste into the UE project: comments plus UPROPERTYs that do not compile outside a class
- agree a target format with the UE side, then generate real rows

## Expected impact
The Encounter tab export becomes an actual hand-off. Verifying it needs the UE project.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - export importable by UE
Before: 0 importable rows for N placed enemies
After: N
Method: simulation - verification needs a UE headless import (operator-only act)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
instrument: UE headless import of the generated asset and a row-count check against the placed enemies
